findings.body:
Line 4 now discards the result of write_all with `let _ =`. save() then returns only the result of flush() on line 5. For writers whose flush is a no-op, such as std::fs::File and TcpStream, flush returns Ok even when write_all failed, so a failed write (for example ENOSPC on a full disk or a reset connection) is reported as success.

Trigger: Calling save() with a writer whose write_all fails but whose flush succeeds, such as a File on a full disk or a socket that errors on write.)

Impact: Any caller that relies on save() returning Err for a failed write now gets Ok(()) with the record missing. The change silently breaks the io::Result contract and causes silent data loss.
findings.title: write_all error discarded in save(), so failed writes report success

risk_level.reason: The change discards the error from write_all with `let _ =`, so a failed or partial write is silently ignored and save() still reports success via flush, risking silent data loss.
